findings.evidence: `nl` shows `@[expose, implicit_reducible]` at line 312 and `@[expose] noncomputable def tensor` at line 337; the same file has `TensorProduct_coact` at line 325, `tensor_toLinearMap` at line 351, and `tensor_tmul` at line 364.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` from both definitions and keep the public characterization lemmas as the supported API.
findings.issue: `Comodule.TensorProduct` and `Comodule.Hom.tensor` are marked `@[expose]`, exposing their structure bodies even though the observable data is already exported by `TensorProduct_coact`, `tensor_toLinearMap`, and `tensor_tmul`.

findings.evidence: `rg -n "theorem tensor_(toLinearMap|tmul|id|comp)|def tensor" ...` returns only `def tensor`, `tensor_toLinearMap`, and `tensor_tmul`; there are no `tensor_id` or `tensor_comp` lemmas.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp]` lemmas for tensoring identities and tensoring composites, e.g. `tensor (Hom.id ...) (Hom.id ...) = Hom.id ...` and `tensor (Hom.comp f₂ f₁) (Hom.comp g₂ g₁) = Hom.comp (tensor f₂ g₂) (tensor f₁ g₁)`.
findings.issue: `Comodule.Hom.tensor` lacks characteristic interaction lemmas with the existing morphism operations `Hom.id` and `Hom.comp`, so later functor/category code must reprove basic tensor functor laws from extensionality.

summary: The new tensor-product surface exposes implementation bodies that are already characterized by public lemmas, and the morphism tensor API is missing the functorial simp lemmas consumers need for the next categorical layer.
